title: Lifting etale inverse-image sections from an inverse limit
statement: Let $I$ be nonempty and directed, $D:I^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Scheme}$ a system of qcqs schemes with affine transition morphisms, and $c$ a limit cone [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Choose $i_0\in I$, a sheaf of sets $G$ on $D(i_0)$, and a quasi-compact quasi-separated etale object $W_0$ over $D(i_0)$. For every section $t$ of the inverse image of $G$ on $W_0\times_{D(i_0)}c.pt$, there are an object $j$ of $\mathrm{Over}(i_0^{\mathrm{op}})$ and a section $s$ of the inverse image at that stage such that the canonical cone section comparison [def-weil-pbc-sets-section-comparison] maps $s$ to $t$.

source.place: Theorem Tag 09YQ (theorem-colimit), degree zero for sheaves of sets; proof via Tags 0EYL, 04HR, 09YN and the finite affine-cover reduction for qcqs schemes

proof.text: Pass to the cofinal upper tail. Transition maps are affine by hypothesis and limit projections are affine by the limit-affine theorem (transport from its chosen limit to c). Use the affine-etale site colimit and restriction equivalences. The unit-compatible affine inverse-image comparison transports the sheaves and their transition isomorphisms to this site presentation. Composition identifies the inverse-image sheaves at the limit with a constant system, whose colimit is that inverse image by connectedness. The colimit-of-sites sections theorem therefore identifies the filtered colimit of affine stage sections with the limit sections, with the displayed unit/composition maps.

For affine W0 the section comparison bijection gives a stage representative of any limit section. For general W0 choose a finite affine etale cover and finite affine refinements of pairwise overlaps. Lift the finitely many restrictions by the affine result, and move them to one common stage. Their overlap restrictions agree at the limit. Apply eventual equality to each of the finitely many overlap refinements, and move these equalities to a single later stage. Separatedness on the refinements makes the lifted covering sections compatible on the overlaps. The sheaf gluing condition gives a section on the entire descended W0; its limit image equals the original section by separatedness. Empty covers produce the unique section.
